title: A section-compatible tensor-pullback comparison is an isomorphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $M,N$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules. Use the tensor-formula pullback $f^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and write $f^*s=\eta_M(s)$ for the unit of the canonical adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Suppose $\alpha:f^*(M\otimes N)\to f^*M\otimes f^*N$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules such that, for every open $V\subseteq Y$ and sections $s\in M(V)$ and $t\in N(V)$, $\alpha_{f^{-1}V}(f^*(s\otimes t))=f^*s\otimes f^*t$. Then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. No naturality in $M,N$ is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The stalk functor [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] and the pullback-stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback], followed by extension of the tensor-stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor], give $\lambda:(f^*(M\otimes N))_x\cong B\otimes_A(M_y\otimes_A N_y)$. Tensor-stalk identification on $X$, followed by the tensor of the two pullback-stalk identifications, gives $\rho:(f^*M\otimes f^*N)_x\cong(B\otimes_A M_y)\otimes_B(B\otimes_A N_y)$. Both preserve the recorded pure-tensor germ formulas.

Represent $s_y\in M_y$ and $t_y\in N_y$ by sections over opens $U,V$ containing $y$, then restrict to $U\cap V$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The pure-tensor germ formula for $\lambda$ gives $\lambda((f^*(s\otimes t))_x)=1\otimes(s_y\otimes t_y)$. The hypothesis on $\alpha$, functoriality of germs, and the germ formula for $\rho$ give $\rho(\alpha_x((f^*(s\otimes t))_x))=(1\otimes s_y)\otimes(1\otimes t_y)$. Therefore $\lambda^{-1};\alpha_x;\rho$ agrees on $1\otimes(s_y\otimes t_y)$ with the base-change tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-tensor-distrib]. Tensor induction and $B$-linearity give equality on every element.

The equality in the preceding step writes $\alpha_x$ as a composite of the three displayed isomorphisms, hence $\alpha_x$ is an isomorphism. Since this holds for every $x$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] implies that $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. In Lean forget the stalk module action, apply the abelian-sheaf stalk criterion and reflect isomorphisms through Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf.
